frame.runs_fingerprint_rule: sha1 over path:mtime_ns:size of the consumed *.eval_results.json files (since 2026-09-02; before: every file under runs/)
frame.inputs_content_rule:
sha256 (first 12 hex) of the UTF-8 bytes of lines `<arm>	<task>	<passes>	<attempts>
` for every consumed cell (every sampled arm, kept tasks only; arm = the fail matrix's `model` column verbatim; passes = attempts - fails, fails counted under plus_status), lines sorted as plain strings by (arm, task) — reproducible from artifacts/fail_counts_matrix.csv; reference script data/inputs_content_sha.py
frame.rebuild_condition: re-pulls when failure-vs-difficulty's board handoff changes (each landing) or the Bayesian/capability_C chains re-emit; frame is a snapshot at build_ts

fit_set.method: sha256 (hex) over the UTF-8 bytes of the elements_of_record leaf's lines '<arm_id>\t<sha12>' — the leaf's own keys, one line per entry, sorted bytewise by arm_id, joined by '\n' with no trailing newline — the identity of the SERVED SET, moving with every row added, replaced or re-bound; n_served_elements beside it is the count to check against the table's rows (fit-methods' word of 12:0xZ 12 Oct 2026 on capability-vs-reliability's fact; fitting). set_sha256 and n_result_files keep their wave meaning: they count the posterior files in results_dir, not the served set.
fit_set.set_sha256_method: sha256 over sorted(basename + bytes) of the SERVED posterior_summary_*.json files (not_served stems excluded; n_arms counts the same files) — counts the posterior files in results_dir and not the served set, whose identity is served_elements_sha256 (12 Oct 2026)

gates.convention: FAIL iff divergences/(chains×samples) > 0.5% or R-hat gate not pass or ESS gate FAIL (bayes-refits DATA-CONTRACTS)
gates.line: sampler gate (0.5%-of-draws convention): 42 of 58 pass · max divergence share 0.09% · R-hat ≤ 1.044 · bulk-ESS ≥ 121
